newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Ex-Soviet Georgia expects record wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet Georgia expects record wheat crop.

text.p: Ex-Soviet Georgia is forecasting a record post-independence wheat crop of over 300,000 tonnes in 1997, an official from the Agriculture and Food Ministry said on Monday.
Deputy Minister Simon Uzunashvili forecast output at 304,154 tonnes, far above the 179,000 harvested in 1996 and 1995's 125,000 tonnes.
He said 229,000 tonnes would be for human consumption and the rest was feed grain, but imports would still be needed.
"The situation is much better this year, because seeds and fertiliser were brought to sowing areas in time," he said. He gave no forecasts for output of other grains.
In 1994/95 annual consumption fell to 600,000 tonnes.
Georgia imported over 300,000 tonnes of wheat last year, mostly in the form of humanitarian aid and shipments from former Soviet republics, including Russia, Kazakhstan and Ukraine.
Georgia no longer levies value-added tax or customs duties on grain imports.
